data.title: The AI Trade Is Shifting From Chip Stocks to Cybersecurity — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Paul R. La Monica

So much for the so-called SaaSpocalypse.

Shares of large software-as-a-service companies, such as cybersecurity firms CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks — a Barron's stock pick in June — were among the top-performing stocks in the S&P 500 this week, with each surging more than 10% during a volatile couple of days for the tech sector and broader market. Elsewhere in the software sector, ServiceNow and Workday each also rose more than 10%.

Meanwhile, chip stocks got crushed. Semiconductor equipment company Lam Research plunged 13% this week after warning of supply constraints. It's another sign that the landscape for winners and losers in the artifical-intelligence trade is constantly shifting. Several other semiconductor companies, including Lam rival KLA and AI chip and infrastructure firms Cerebras Systems and Credo Technology, all fell more than 10%.

Meanwhile, the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector exchange-traded fund and the First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF rose 6% and 7% this week, respectively, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell 3%. (The broader market ended the week mixed, with the Dow notching a 0.4% gain and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq marking respective losses of 0.5% and 0.7%.)

Investors, at least for now, seem to be gravitating toward companies that are expected to get a big boost in demand thanks to AI. Think cybersecurity as worries about data breaches and other concerns about rogue AI agents mount. Enterprise software firms are rebounding following a slide earlier this year due to fears — that now appear to have been overblown — about how AI could make big corporate software firms obsolete.

Meanwhile, there are growing concerns among investors that the rally in chip stocks and other hardware companies — which have been viewed as the biggest beneficiary of hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet investing heavily in AI — needs to cool off a bit.

Along those lines, shares of hard drive maker Western Digital fell Friday despite reporting solid earnings. The stock is up nearly 100% this year.

Investors should get more clarity about how this dynamic in the tech stock trade is unfolding in the coming week. Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet are all due to report quarterly earnings. So are ServiceNow, cybersecurity firm Fortinet, KLA, Western Digital competitor Seagate, plus Intel and Sandisk.

Sandisk, for example, is expected to report a year-over-year sales increase of more than 360% and an earnings per share surge of nearly 3,700% from a year ago. Those are not misprints. Demand is booming for Sandisk's flash memory drives due to AI.

Could this growth be enough to satisfy investors? Sandisk shares are up more than 420% this year, and the stock is the second-best performer in the S&P 500. But shares fell nearly 5% last week and have plunged more than 30% in the past month.

As earnings season continues, great results may not be enough to shift the scales back towards AI hardware stocks.

data.title: Six Flags adding seat belts to roller coasters following Georgia park death
data.description:
Key points:
  • Six Flags Entertainment CEO John Reilly on Friday said that seat belts would be added to the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia, after a man fell off the ride to his death earlier this month.
  • He added that similar coasters at its other parks would also get the seatbelts. Hypercoasters such as Goliath already have a clamshell lap bar restraint.
  • "We have engaged independent engineers and ride inspection specialists to comprehensively review current safety procedures across our entire portfolio of rides and attractions, across all of our parks," Reilly wrote in his message to guests and passholders.

data.title: Accuser in Cornell rape allegations can stay anonymous, judge rules
data.description:
By Milana Vinn

The woman at the center of rape allegations against Cornell University students can keep using a pseudonym in her lawsuit, a judge ruled.

  • New York state Judge Phaedra Perry-Bond ruled on Friday that the accuser's privacy interests, particularly concerns for her safety, outweighed the need to publicly disclose her identity in court proceedings.

  • The woman, who alleges she was drugged and raped by Cornell University students in 2024, has been the target of threats, her lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, said earlier this month.

  • Although the defendants in the lawsuit did not oppose the request for anonymity, Perry-Bond wrote that "some members of the public have made it their mission to try and identify Jane Doe."

  • The judge warned that "cyberstalking and engaging in or encouraging threats across state lines, whether it be of Jane Doe, of any of the named defendants, or their attorneys, can be considered a federal crime and perpetrators of those acts may be subjecting themselves to prosecution."

  • The woman, who was 20 at the time of the alleged gang rape, filed her suit on September 16, prompting prosecutors to reopen a criminal investigation they had initially closed ​without charges.

data.title: WULF Stock Hits Six-Month Weekly Low As TeraWulf Secures Larger Credit Line For AI Data Center Expansion
data.description:
Key points:
  • TeraWulf shares saw the lowest weekly level over the six months, as the stock fell over 60% since June.
  • The company announced on Friday that its senior secured resolving credit facility from $250 million to $400 million.
  • TeraWulf signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic for approximately 401 megawatts of IT capacity at its Justified Data Campus.

TeraWulf Inc. (WULF) stock closed at its lowest weekly level in at least six months on Friday. This continued a drop that has wiped out more than 60% of the stock's value since June. The company announced it increased its senior secured revolving credit facility by about 60% to about $400 million. This gives the company more borrowing power as it builds data centers for AI clients.

According to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the Easton, Maryland-based company changed the facility on Friday to increase total commitments from $250 million right away. In this case, Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. is both the administrative agent and the collateral agent.

WULF stock closed at $11.32, down 3.1% this week, trading between $11.07 and $13.05 during the week. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around WULF remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, accompanied by ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.

TeraWulf’s Revolver Gains Expansion Option

The amendment adds "an uncommitted accordion" feature that lets commitments go up by another $150 million, but only if more lenders agree to lend more money and other conditions are met. It also gets rid of a $150 million limit that was put on letters of credit.

TeraWulf said it would include the full revised agreement with its report for the three months ending September 30.

The revolver facility is expected to mature in April 2030. At the time, Patrick Fleury, the company's chief financial officer, said a widely syndicated credit facility was a major step forward for how the business operated. The deal was signed on May 7 and closed with $250 million of locked-in capacity.

Morgan Stanley Arranges TeraWulf’s Key Financings

Morgan Stanley has been a key lender in TeraWulf's growth. In October 2025, the bank was the only bookrunner for a $3.2 billion senior secured notes offering by subsidiary WULF Compute. The money raised helped pay for part of an expansion of the company's data center at its Lake Mariner campus in New York.

Morgan Stanley is also the administrative agent on a separate $500 million, 364-day delayed-draw bridge facility, which finances TeraWulf’s data center in Hawesville, Kentucky.

TeraWulf Expands Anthropic Deal, Sells Abernathy Stake

The company signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic (ANTHZZX) for about 401 megawatts of critical IT capacity at its Justified Data Campus in Kentucky. TeraWulf's added liquidity comes as it takes on bigger projects.

TeraWulf said that the lease will bring in about $19 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term, and up to about $33 billion if both five-year extensions are exercised. The company also agreed to sell its 50.1% share of the Abernathy joint venture for cash worth around $530 million.

data.title: CBI books Mumbai company for Canara bank fraud of Rs. 212.34 crores
data.description:
Accused persons entered into a criminal conspiracy, obtained term loan of Rs.100 crore from Erstwhile Syndicate Bank (now Canara Bank), LCB Branch, Mumbai and USD 50 Million from London Branch : CBI

New Delhi, October 24: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered a case on the complaint of Canara Bank, Circle Office, Bandra (East), Mumbai, against M/s IL & FS Energy Development Company Limited and its Managing Directors / Directors,

CBI has booked Sunil Wadhwa, Anoop Seth, Hari Sankaran, Ramesh Chandra Bawa, Arun Kumar Saha, unknown public servants and unknown private persons for offenses of criminal conspiracy for cheating and also the  offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act, resulting in alleged wrongful loss of Rs. 212.34 crore to the complainant bank.

It has been alleged that the accused persons entered into a criminal conspiracy, obtained term loan of Rs.100 crore from Erstwhile Syndicate Bank (now Canara Bank), LCB Branch, Mumbai and USD 50 Million from London Branch. The company defrauded the bank by not utilizing the bank funds for the intended purpose for which it was sanctioned. Further, it is alleged that the company diverted the funds by siphoning off through associate companies and caused loss to the bank.

The CBI conducted searches at multiple premises linked to the Managing Directors / Directors of M/s IL & FS Energy Development Company Limited in Mumbai, Delhi and Noida etc.

CBI stated that during the searches, incriminating bank documents, deposit slips, mutual funds portfolio documents, bank account / property details of the directors and Ledgers of the company etc. relevant to the investigation were recovered and seized.

data.title: Adani Wind Third-Party Orders Cross 1 GW With 696 MW New Wins
data.description:
The orders include projects from NTPC Renewable Energy, Jindal India Power, Purvah Green Power and other major producers

Adani Wind, the wind energy business of Adani New Industries, has secured 696.2 MW of orders from five power producers as it expands its customer base beyond the Adani Group amid growing demand for higher-capacity wind turbines.

The orders include 300 MW from Purvah Green Power, 155 MW from Jindal India Power, 109.2 MW from NTPC Renewable Energy, 82.5 MW from Aditya Birla Renewables and 49.5 MW from Integrum Energy. The projects will use 5.2 MW, 5 MW and 3.3 MW turbine platforms across Karnataka, Gujarat and Maharashtra, according to sources cited in a media report.

Purvah Green Power, part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, has placed the largest order at 300 MW. The contract covers 60 turbines of Adani Wind's 5 MW platform for deployment in Bellary, Karnataka. Jindal India Power, part of the BC Jindal Group, has ordered 155 MW through 31 turbines of the same 5 MW platform. The machines are planned for installation in Davanagere, Karnataka.

NTPC Renewable Energy has ordered 21 turbines rated at 5.2 MW each for its Khavda project in Gujarat. Aditya Birla Renewables and Integrum Energy will use Adani Wind's 3.3 MW platform for projects in Bhuj, Gujarat, and Nandurbar, Maharashtra, respectively.

Manufacturing Capacity Expansion

The latest orders have taken Adani Wind's cumulative order book from independent power producers outside the Adani Group beyond 1 GW. The company is seeking to strengthen its third-party business as India's wind market expands and turbine manufacturers compete for new projects.

As per the report, Adani Wind is also planning to raise annual manufacturing capacity at its Mundra facility in Gujarat from 2.25 GW to 5 GW. The company has set a longer-term target of reaching 10 GW of annual capacity, which could support both domestic demand and overseas opportunities.

The company's 5 MW MWL-185 turbine has a rotor diameter of 185 metres and a hub height of 140 metres and is designed for low- to moderate-wind conditions. Its 5.2 MW MWL-160 is among the higher-capacity onshore turbine models included in the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy's Approved List of Models and Manufacturers.

Wind Industry Scales Up

India had 59.2 GW of installed wind power capacity, with another 43 GW under implementation, taking the combined operational and under-development capacity beyond 100 GW.

Domestic wind turbine manufacturing capacity has more than doubled from around 12 GW in fiscal 2023 to over 24 GW annually. The industry is targeting installations of around 8 GW in fiscal 2027, while annual additions are projected to reach 13.2 GW by fiscal 2031.

data.title: Pfizer's 25-Valent Pediatric Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine Candidate Shows Robust Phase 2 Data at IDWeek 2026
data.description:
Pfizer Inc. () today announced detailed results across serotypes from a Phase 2 study (NCT06524414) for its investigational 25-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine candidate, PF-07872412 (25vPnC), in infants. In the study, a four-dose series of 25vPnC elicited robust immune responses against all 25 serotypes and showed safety and tolerability comparable to four doses of PREVNAR 20® (Pneumococcal 20-valent Conjugate Vaccine). These findings were shared today in an oral presentation at IDWeek 2026 in Washington, D.C.1

These data support the ongoing Phase 3 development program for 25vPnC, which, if successful, could help provide protection against serotypes collectively responsible for approximately 84% of invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) cases among children under five years of age in the U.S.2

“These encouraging data build on more than 25 years of progress in protecting children from serious pneumococcal disease with PREVNAR vaccines. By expanding serotype coverage and applying next-generation technology to the historically challenging serotype 3, this candidate aims to extend the substantial reductions in disease that existing vaccines have achieved. If successful, it could help provide children with the broadest protection against invasive pneumococcal disease to date.”

— Annaliesa Anderson, Ph.D., Senior Vice President and Chief Vaccines Officer, Pfizer

Phase 2 Study Results Across 25 Serotypes

The Phase 2 study is evaluating the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of the 25-valent vaccine candidate (25vPnC) compared with PREVNAR 20 in healthy infants. These data build on results announced earlier this year showing:

  • Robust immune responses against all 25 serotypes one month after Dose 3 and one month after Dose 4, including against all five new serotypes (15A, 23A, 23B, 24F, and 35B). Rates of local reactions, systemic events, and adverse events were balanced across the 25-valent vaccine candidate and PREVNAR 20 groups in the Phase 2 trial. Adverse events were consistent with conditions commonly diagnosed in this age group. There were no related serious adverse events identified in the study. 1

  • The 25-valent vaccine candidate elicited an enhanced immune response against serotype 3 compared with PREVNAR 20, generating GMCs that were 8.8-fold higher one month after Dose 3 and approximately 15-fold higher one month after Dose 4. 1 It utilizes next-generation technology specifically designed to elicit a more robust immune response against serotype 3, which accounts for 10.6% of all IPD in children under five years old in the U.S. 2

  • 25-valent vaccine candidate also elicited functional responses in the opsonophagocytic activity assay (OPA) one month after Dose 4 for all 25 target serotypes, demonstrating booster effects. 1 This result demonstrates the vaccine candidate’s potential to generate antibodies that can contribute to the functional killing of pneumococcal bacteria.3

Detailed results from the presentation can be found online here.

Continuing Pfizer’s Commitment to Pneumococcal Disease Prevention

These results build on Pfizer’s long-standing commitment to protecting people from pneumococcal disease. Pfizer is advancing two next-generation pneumococcal conjugate vaccine candidates across pediatric and adult populations.

  • In children, 25vPnC is being evaluated in three Phase 3 studies that began earlier in 2026, with up to 6,830 participants randomized to receive 25vPnC or PREVNAR 20.4,5,6 Additionally, Pfizer has completed enrollment of a Phase 3 study to demonstrate the consistency of three manufacturing lots of 25vPnC.7

  • The five new serotypes (15A, 23A, 23B, 24F, and 35B) are estimated to account for an additional ~30% of pediatric invasive pneumococcal disease cases in the U.S. compared with PREVNAR 20.2 It also uses next-generation technology designed to improve responses to serotype 3, which accounts for 10.6% of invasive pneumococcal disease in U.S. children under five years of age.1,2

  • In adults, Pfizer plans to bring a fifth-generation, 35-valent vaccine candidate into clinical development by the end of 2026, pending alignment from regulatory authorities.

For more information on Pfizer’s Commitment to Vaccines, please visit: Vaccines | Pfizer | Pfizer. More information on Pfizer’s overall presence at IDWeek 2026 is here.

U.S. INDICATION AND IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION FOR PREVNAR 20

INDICATION

PREVNAR 20 is a vaccine approved for:

  • the prevention of invasive disease caused by 20 Streptococcus pneumoniae strains (1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 8, 9V, 10A, 11A, 12F, 14, 15B, 18C, 19A, 19F, 22F, 23F, and 33F) in individuals 6 weeks of age and older.

  • the prevention of otitis media (middle ear infection) caused by 7 of the 20 strains in individuals 6 weeks through 5 years.

  • active immunization for the prevention of pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae strains 1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 8, 9V, 10A, 11A, 12F, 14, 15B, 18C, 19A, 19F, 22F, 23F, and 33F in individuals 18 years of age and older.

The indication for the prevention of pneumonia caused by S. pneumoniae serotypes 8, 10A, 11A, 12F, 15B, 22F, and 33F in individuals 18 years of age and older is approved based on immune responses. Continued approval may depend on a supportive study.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

  • PREVNAR 20 should not be given to anyone who has had a severe allergic reaction to any component of Prevnar 20 or to diphtheria toxoid.

  • Individuals with weakened immune systems may have a lower immune response. Safety data are not available for these groups.

  • A temporary pause in breathing after getting a vaccine has been observed in some infants who were born prematurely. For premature infants, talk to your healthcare provider about the infant's medical status when deciding to get vaccinated with Prevnar 20.

  • In individuals 2, 4, 6, and 12 through 15 months of age vaccinated with a 4-dose schedule, the most common side effects reported at a rate of >10% were irritability, pain at the injection site, drowsiness, decreased appetite, injection site redness, injection site swelling, and fever.

  • In individuals 15 months through 17 years of age vaccinated with a single dose, the most common side effects reported at a rate of >10% were irritability, pain at the injection site, drowsiness, fatigue, muscle pain, decreased appetite, injection site swelling, injection site redness, headache, and fever.

  • In individuals 18 years and older, the most common side effects reported at a rate of >10% were pain at the injection site, muscle pain, fatigue, headache, and joint pain. Also, injection site swelling was common in individuals 18 years through 59 years of age.

  • Ask your healthcare provider about the risks and benefits of Prevnar 20. Only a healthcare provider can decide if PREVNAR 20 is right for you or your child.

data.title: Sygnum Launches Bitcoin Loans With Collateral Keys Shared Across Parties
data.description:
TL;DR: Sygnum and Debifi have launched MultiSYG, a Bitcoin-backed lending service using segregated multisignature wallets. The arrangement spreads control of collateral across several parties, while borrowers remain exposed to the economics of a secured loan.

Sygnum and Debifi launched MultiSYG on October 23, bringing shared control of Bitcoin collateral into the bank’s lending business. Each borrower receives a dedicated wallet with keys distributed among several parties.

In their launch announcement, the companies described a structure involving the client, Sygnum Bank and independent institutional key holders. Transactions require valid signatures under the wallet’s Bitcoin Script rules, so compromising one key would not be enough to move the collateral.

The service arrives as Bitcoin becomes more prominent in Sygnum’s lending book. The bank says the asset now represents more than 80% of pledged collateral volume, compared with 63% in 2023. Those figures describe the bank’s own clients, rather than the entire crypto lending market.

Shared Keys Change The Custody Arrangement

Sygnum’s product information says MultiSYG holdings and movements can be checked on-chain. Its broader lending description says collateral remains client-owned, off the bank’s balance sheet and bankruptcy remote.

That is a more specific proposition than a general promise to keep funds safe. A borrower can examine where the coins sit, while the signing arrangement distributes the authority needed to spend them.

But shared signatures and shared commercial interests are different things. An independent key holder’s role depends on the agreed process. The launch release does not specify the exact signing threshold, interest rate or loan-to-value limit, leaving those details to the product documentation and client agreement.

For readers comparing custody models, this means counting keys alone gives an incomplete picture. Who may authorise a transfer, under which circumstances and through what recovery procedure matters just as much.

The Loan Still Has A Margin Requirement

The broader lending information describes credit that lets clients obtain fiat liquidity without an immediate sale of their crypto. It says collateral remains client-owned unless a credit event occurs, with continuous risk monitoring and margin management.

The bank also says pledged assets are not rehypothecated. Its general lending terms describe interest accruing daily on the utilised balance and restrict transfers of locked collateral, while allowing access to excess collateral.

These conditions explain why wallet security cannot remove borrowing risk. If collateral falls in value, the lender’s required coverage can become harder to maintain. A borrower may need more collateral or less outstanding debt, regardless of how securely the existing coins are held.

Similarly, obtaining cash without selling on an exchange preserves exposure to future Bitcoin price moves in both directions. The debt and interest bill continue to exist alongside that exposure.

MultiSYG therefore changes the control and visibility of pledged assets. Whether the loan suits a particular treasury still turns on its cash needs, financing cost and ability to respond when collateral values change.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: SA Asks: How can General Motors get back on track?
data.description:
Shares of General Motors slid significantly this week after the legacy automaker released a weaker-than-expected forecast, fanning concerns about the company's rising costs and product strategy.

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Daniel Jones and Bernard Zambonin how they thought GM could get back on track.

Daniel Jones: This year has not been particularly pleasant for General Motors shareholders. The car giant has seen its share price drop significantly at a time when the market is up double digits. Global car production is down about 1%. In the U.S. it is up a surprising 1.4%, but in other parts of the world, it is falling rather rapidly. In China, for instance, it has fallen 5.8%.

But even though the U.S., which is where GM gets a lot of its value, is doing surprisingly well in the automotive production space, the company is losing ground. It has seen its market share go from 17.3% in the first half of last year to just 16.7% during the same period this year.

In China, GM's market share has fallen from 7.2% to 6.8%. And in the Asia Pacific, Middle East, and Africa combined region, its market share has fallen from 4.7% to 4.2%. Only in South America is the company doing surprisingly well, with market share virtually flat. But that accounts for just a small slice of its overall output.

A year ago, the company was doing far better. I would say that a lot of its recent pain can be attributed to its decision to scale back drastically on electric vehicles. Citing weakening demand in the final quarter of last year, the company took a $6B charge related to its EV investing plans. 

Some of this scale-back may have made sense. After all, the U.S. government ended the $7,500 EV tax credit in September. But now, with oil prices skyrocketing because of the war against Iran, the decision looks like a bad one.

In a relatively short period of time, the company went from being a marginal player in the EV space to being the second largest in the U.S. In Q3 2024, it had a market share of 9.3%, up from 6.1% a year earlier. By Q3 2025, it had ballooned to 15.2%. The latest data that we have covers the final quarter of last year, and in such a short window of time, it had dropped to 10.8%. Almost certainly, it is lower now.

At the same time, EV sales are rising in the U.S. The third quarter of this year saw a total output of 262,649 vehicles, 6.1% higher than what we saw for the second quarter.

There's also the longer-term picture. According to one analysis, by 2030, EV sales in the U.S. will account for up to 38% of new car sales.

Management made a long-term decision based on short-term conditions, and shareholders are now paying the price. Reversing that course of action and remaining committed to it is the best path forward for the business to create value for investors.

(Daniel Jones runs the SA investment newsletter Crude Value Insights.)

data.title: Looking for AI stocks that are still cheap? Consider these two under-the-radar picks.
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

Simon Kim of Saturna Capital names two stocks tied to base metals, for investors who want to look beyond the beaten path for AI-related trades

Komatsu trades much lower relative to sales and earnings estimates than larger rival Caterpillar.

Simon Kim and his co-managers for the Saturna International Fund believe that the artificial-intelligence build-out still has a long way to go, despite market jitters over high valuations. So they are still "overweight AI" but are looking for stocks in related industries that trade at attractive valuations.

The Saturna International Fund SSIFX is rated five stars (the highest rating) within Morningstar's "Foreign Large Growth" category. As of Sept. 30, about 15% of the 40-stock portfolio was invested in U.S. companies, according to Morningstar's data.

During an interview with MarketWatch, Kim named Komatsu (KMTUY) (JP:6301), the Japan-based manufacturer of heavy construction equipment, as an example of a value-priced investment tied to base metals, which he described as an industry that is "tangential to AI."

"Within base metals, there are not a lot of good companies," he said, because mining firms and financiers "have destroyed capital by investing heavily at the wrong times."

'They sit back and collect.'Simon Kim of the Saturna International Fund, on the business strategy of Altius Minerals

"What I am looking for is companies that track the metals price and have compounding alpha on top of that," Kim said.

"You get exposure to the metals price. If the supercycle hits, these companies will benefit," and, if not, you still hold compounding businesses at reasonable valuations, he said.

"Alpha" refers to how much something outperforms its benchmark or market average.

Komatsu and Caterpillar

The Saturna International Fund holds shares of Komatsu that are listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. There is also an American depositary receipt for the company.

Komatsu is Caterpillar's (CAT) main international competitor, although it is a much smaller company, with a market capitalization of $42.6 billion and a consensus 2026 revenue estimate of $28.18 billion for its fiscal year that will end in March, according to a FactSet survey of analysts. In comparison, Caterpillar's market cap is $333.63 billion, and its annual sales for 2026 are estimated to total $79.95 billion.

If we look at the stock price relative to forward sales estimates, based on consensus estimates for the next 12 months among analysts pooled by FactSet, Komatsu's ADR trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 1.5, while Caterpillar's stock price is 3.8 times forward sales. And the forward price-to-earnings ratio for Komatsu's ADR is 15, while Caterpillar's forward P/E is 23, according to FactSet.

Now take a look at a one-year chart, which shows better performance for Caterpillar, but a lot less volatility for Komatsu:

Caterpillar's stock has had a higher return than Komatsu's ADR over the past year, but it has been a bumpier ride for "CAT."

For one-year total returns though Monday, with dividends reinvested, Caterpillar takes the prize. But so far in 2026, Komatsu's ADR has returned 47.5%, while Caterpillar has returned 27.5%.

Over the past three years, Caterpillar's stock has returned 202%, while Komatsu's ADR has returned 92%.

According to Kim, Caterpillar "has shot up from power generation, since they sell backup generators (and now primary) for data centers, and demand has been ferocious," while Caterpillar's other business lines have also performed well.

"Komatsu does the same things, except that they are not selling the generators," he said.

Kim estimated that the market was placing a $200 billion valuation on Caterpillar's generator business. According to Caterpillar, power-generation equipment sales were $3.1 billion during the second quarter, providing 15% of total revenue, which came to $20.54 billion.

Kim said Caterpillar's power-generation segment could contribute 20% to 25% of the company's total sales next year, but he is still surprised that the market has been "valuing the rest of the biz at $150 billion."

"So it is either valuing [Caterpillar] incorrectly or Komatsu has some catching up to do."

A royalty play

Kim said that the Saturna International Fund tends to hold stocks for about eight years. He cited Altius Minerals, which is based in St. John's, Newfoundland, as an example of a company that has taken an opportunistic long-term approach to provide financing to mining firms at excellent terms during down periods. The company's main stock listing is on the Toronto Stock Exchange (CA:ALS), but the stock is also traded over-the-counter in the U.S. (ATUSF).

According to Kim, Altius's contrarian strategy under its co-founder and CEO Brian Dalton in the base-metals space has led the strong performance for its stock over long periods. These are total returns through Monday:

 
Company                               2026  3 years  5 years  10 years  20 years 
Altius Minerals (Toronto listing     36.4%     183%     258%      482%      893% 
Altius Minerals (U.S. OTC            32.3%     173%     216%      445%      693% 
S&P 500                              13.4%      87%      83%      323%      722% 
                                                                 Source: FactSet

You can see that the U.S. over-the-counter shares of Altius haven't performed as well as the main listing on the Toronto exchange. The U.S. OTC shares trade in much lower volumes.

"This is the same business model as a Franco or Wheaton - the royalty model. These companies provide capital to a miner in exchange for future revenues," Kim said, referring to Franco-Nevada (FNV) and Wheaton Precious Metas (WPM).

"They want to use capital when commodity prices are low, and people are looking for cash and they are desperate and giving good terms," he said.

"The interesting thing about this royalty model is it has outperformed base metals, as a sector, over the past couple of decades," he said.

Kim cited down cycles for base metals in 2016 and following Russia's invasion of Ukraine as examples of market disruptions that Altius was able to take advantage of.

"They sit back and collect" while waiting for new opportunities, he said.

Kim said the latest example was in the renewable-energy space. "In 2022 you had all these wind investments, and other power generators starved for capital," while at that time Altius, under Dalton's direction, "was buying up assets left and right."

Subsequent events "proved he was right" because of heavy demand for power for data centers, Kim said.

When asked about the high forward P/E of 54.5 for Altius's stock, which compares with a weighted valuation of 18.9 for the S&P 500 SPX, Kim said that for a mining royalty stock, price-to-book value is a more reasonable way to look at valuations. Altius trades at 2.3 times book value, while the S&P 500 trades at 5.6 times book, according to FactSet.

-Philip van Doorn

Oppenheimer upgraded Zoom Communications to Outperform from Perform with a $130 price target.

“We are upgrading ZM from Perform to Outperform with a $130 price target as we gain confidence in its transition from video meetings to a broader AI communications and workflow platform,” Oppenheimer analyst Timothy Horan wrote.

Delving deeper, Horan said the company's AI Platform has its own unique data, AI models and comes with “excellent security and governance.” It also combines meetings, productivity apps, unified communications and contact center, along with ZoomMate.

Apple downgraded on iPhone shipment concerns

Loop Capital downgraded Apple to Hold from Buy, citing concerns about a cut in iPhone shipments.

“The gist is that when AAPL previously reduced its Sep Q & Dec Q iPhone unit ships by 10% we believed they would be in a position to make up many (if not most) of these units through CY2027 as the reductions were supply related (memory & processors) & not demand related,” Loop Capital analyst Ananda Baruah wrote, adding that “this no longer appears to be the case.”

“We continue to like AAPL’s longer-term share gain and Services story… but believe the stock also requires a fundamental catalyst reset after its recent stock appreciation... particularly given its trading at 5-year valuation highs as iPhone ships have been reduced and [gross margin] could see incremental pressure,” the analyst added.

Alcoa is having trouble overcoming the pricing pressures, prompting Argus analyst Alexandra Yates to reduce her rating until seeing more of a rebound in the market driven by long-term sustainable demand.

data.title: IMFINZI® (durvalumab) plus tarlatamab-dlle reduced the risk of death by 58% in 1st-line extensive-stage small cell lung cancer in the DeLLphi-305 Phase III trial
data.description:
Landmark results from the DeLLphi-305 Phase III trial showed IMFINZI® (durvalumab) plus Amgen’s tarlatamab-dlle demonstrated a statistically significant and highly clinically meaningful improvement in the primary endpoint of overall survival (OS) and in the key secondary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) versus IMFINZI alone as a 1st-line maintenance treatment. The trial included patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) who had not progressed following standard induction treatment with IMFINZI plus platinum chemotherapy (investigator’s choice of carboplatin or cisplatin) and etoposide.

These results will be presented today in a Proffered Paper session during Presidential Symposium I at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in Madrid, Spain (abstract #LBA3).1 They were also simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

In a planned interim analysis, IMFINZI plus tarlatamab-dlle reduced the risk of death by 58% compared to IMFINZI alone (based on an OS hazard ratio [HR] of 0.42; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.32-0.54; p<0.001) at a median follow-up of approximately 16 months. Median OS was 21.1 months for the combination versus 12.7 months for IMFINZI alone. An estimated 79% of patients treated with the combination were alive at one year compared to 53% for IMFINZI alone.

Results from the key secondary endpoint of PFS showed the combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 66% compared to IMFINZI alone (based on a PFS HR of 0.34; 95% CI 0.28-0.42; p<0.001) at a median follow-up of 13.9 months. Median PFS was 7.4 months for the combination versus 1.9 months for IMFINZI alone. An estimated 38% of patients treated with the combination were alive and had not experienced disease progression at one year compared to 10% for IMFINZI alone.

The OS and PFS benefits observed were consistent across all prespecified subgroups, including patients with brain or liver metastases.

Confirmed objective response rate (ORR) with the combination was six times higher compared to IMFINZI alone (26.4% versus 4.1%; p<0.001). Median duration of response (DOR) for the combination exceeded 1 year (12.7 months) versus 5.6 months for IMFINZI alone.

Jacob Sands, MD, Associate Chief of the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and international coordinating investigator for the trial, said: “For a disease where durable survival has remained extremely difficult to achieve, the magnitude and consistency of benefit in DeLLphi-305 are striking. Importantly, the benefit was seen across clinically relevant groups, including patients with brain metastases. Today’s remarkable results demonstrate substantial progress in our work to achieve meaningfully longer disease control and survival for patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, further highlighting the importance of effective treatment at the earliest possible opportunity.”

Leora Horn, Senior Vice President, Late Development Oncology, Oncology R&D, AstraZeneca, said: “IMFINZI-based induction therapy followed by maintenance treatment with IMFINZI plus tarlatamab-dlle will redefine treatment standards for patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. As the only immunotherapy to demonstrate a significant survival benefit across stages of small cell lung cancer, and now the first in combination with a T-cell engager, these important data further reinforce IMFINZI as the backbone immunotherapy in this setting.”

Severe and Fatal Immune-Mediated Adverse Reactions

Important immune-mediated adverse reactions listed under Warnings and Precautions may not include all possible severe and fatal immune-mediated reactions. Immune-mediated adverse reactions, which may be severe or fatal, can occur in any organ system or tissue. Immune-mediated adverse reactions can occur at any time after starting treatment or after discontinuation. Monitor patients closely for symptoms and signs that may be clinical manifestations of underlying immune-mediated adverse reactions. Evaluate clinical chemistries including liver enzymes, creatinine, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) level, and thyroid function at baseline and before each dose. In cases of suspected immune-mediated adverse reactions, initiate appropriate workup to exclude alternative etiologies, including infection. Institute medical management promptly, including specialty consultation as appropriate. Withhold or permanently discontinue IMFINZI and IMJUDO depending on severity. See USPI Dosing and Administration for specific details. In general, if IMFINZI and IMJUDO requires interruption or discontinuation, administer systemic corticosteroid therapy (1 mg to 2 mg/kg/day prednisone or equivalent) until improvement to Grade 1 or less. Upon improvement to Grade 1 or less, initiate corticosteroid taper and continue to taper over at least 1 month. Consider administration of other systemic immunosuppressants in patients whose immune-mediated adverse reactions are not controlled with corticosteroid therapy.

Complications of Allogeneic HSCT after IMFINZI
Fatal and other serious complications can occur in patients who receive allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) before or after being treated with a PD-1/L-1 blocking antibody. Transplant-related complications include hyperacute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), acute GVHD, chronic GVHD, hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD) after reduced intensity conditioning, and steroid-requiring febrile syndrome (without an identified infectious cause). These complications may occur despite intervening therapy between PD-1/L-1 blockade and allogeneic HSCT. Follow patients closely for evidence of transplant-related complications and intervene promptly. Consider the benefit versus risks of treatment with a PD-1/L-1 blocking antibody prior to or after an allogeneic HSCT.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity
Based on their mechanism of action and data from animal studies, IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus. In females of reproductive potential, verify pregnancy status prior to initiating IMFINZI and IMJUDO and advise them to use effective contraception during treatment with IMFINZI and IMJUDO and for 3 months after the last dose of IMFINZI and IMJUDO.

Lactation
There is no information regarding the presence of IMFINZI and IMJUDO in human milk; however, because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants from IMFINZI and IMJUDO, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose.

Indications:

IMFINZI, as a single agent, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable Stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose disease has not progressed following concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy and radiation therapy (cCRT).

IMFINZI in combination with platinum-containing chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment, followed by IMFINZI continued as a single agent as adjuvant treatment after surgery, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with resectable (tumors ≥4 cm and/or node positive) NSCLC and no known epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations or anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) rearrangements.

IMFINZI, in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic NSCLC with no sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK genomic tumor aberrations.

IMFINZI, as a single agent, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC) whose disease has not progressed following concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy and radiation therapy (cCRT).

IMFINZI, in combination with etoposide and either carboplatin or cisplatin, is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).

IMFINZI, in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer (BTC).

IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).

IMFINZI in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel followed by IMFINZI as a single agent is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer that is mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) as determined by an FDA-authorized test.

IMFINZI in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-naive, high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (HR-NMIBC).

IMFINZI in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin as neoadjuvant treatment, followed by single agent IMFINZI as adjuvant treatment following radical cystectomy, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC).

IMFINZI in combination with fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin and docetaxel (FLOT) as neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment, followed by single agent IMFINZI, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with resectable gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GC/GEJC).

Notes

Small cell lung cancer
Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death globally, accounting for almost one in five (19%) cancer deaths.2,3 Lung cancer is broadly split into non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and SCLC, with about 15% classified as SCLC.4

About two-thirds of SCLC patients are diagnosed with ES-SCLC, a highly aggressive, fast-growing form of lung cancer characterized by rapid tumor progression and metastatic spread to organs such as the brain and liver.5 In 2026, an estimated 195,000 people globally will be treated for ES-SCLC.6

Immune checkpoint inhibitors such as IMFINZI have led to significant improvements in OS in ES-SCLC, establishing a 1st-line standard of care. However, many patients still experience disease progression due to the aggressive nature of the disease, and median OS with the current standard of care is approximately one year.5 Only 18.1% of limited-stage SCLC patients and 3.6% of ES-SCLC patients are alive five years after diagnosis.7

DeLLphi-305
The DeLLphi-305 trial is sponsored by Amgen, with partial funding and IMFINZI provided by AstraZeneca. It is a global Phase III, randomized, open-label clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of IMFINZI in combination with tarlatamab-dlle compared to IMFINZI alone as 1st-line maintenance treatment for patients with ES-SCLC who have not progressed following induction treatment with IMFINZI in combination with platinum chemotherapy and etoposide.

Tarlatamab-dlle is a first-in-class targeted immunotherapy that binds to both DLL3 on tumor cells and CD3 on T cells, thereby activating T cells to kill DLL3-expressing SCLC cells. DLL3 is a protein that is expressed on the surface of SCLC cells in ~85-96% of patients with SCLC, but is minimally expressed on healthy cells.

In the trial, 563 patients who completed IMFINZI -based induction treatment were randomized 1:1 to receive either IMFINZI in combination with tarlatamab-dlle or IMFINZI alone until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Following tarlatamab-dlle infusion on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Cycle 1 Day 8, patients were monitored in a healthcare setting for 1 to 2 hours (6 to 8 hours in certain regions including Europe). The trial included patients with both treated and untreated asymptomatic brain metastases at baseline.

The primary endpoint is OS for IMFINZI plus tarlatamab-dlle versus IMFINZI alone. PFS is a key secondary endpoint.

IMFINZI
IMFINZI® (durvalumab) is a human monoclonal antibody that binds to the PD-L1 protein and blocks the interaction of PD-L1 with the PD-1 and CD80 proteins, countering the tumor’s immune-evading tactics and releasing the inhibition of immune responses.

IMFINZI is the global standard of care based on OS in the curative-intent setting of unresectable, Stage III NSCLC in patients whose disease has not progressed after chemoradiotherapy (CRT). Additionally, IMFINZI is approved as a perioperative treatment in combination with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in resectable NSCLC, and in combination with a short course of IMJUDO (tremelimumab) and chemotherapy for the treatment of metastatic NSCLC. IMFINZI is also approved for limited-stage SCLC and in combination with chemotherapy (etoposide and either carboplatin or cisplatin) for the treatment of ES-SCLC.

IMFINZI is also approved in combination with chemotherapy in locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer and in combination with IMJUDO in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It is also approved as a monotherapy in unresectable HCC in Japan, China and the EU, and in resectable, early-stage and locally advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancers in the US, EU and Japan. Additionally, in April 2026, IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO, lenvatinib and transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in the primary endpoint of PFS versus TACE alone for patients with unresectable HCC eligible for embolization in the EMERALD-3 Phase III trial.

data.title: Perioperative IMFINZI® (durvalumab) plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin reduced risk of recurrence by 49% and risk of death by 42% in muscle-invasive bladder cancer
data.description:
Positive results from the VOLGA Phase III trial showed perioperative treatment with AstraZeneca’s IMFINZI® (durvalumab) in combination with neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin (EV) demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in the primary endpoint of event-free survival (EFS) and key secondary endpoint of overall survival (OS) in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) versus standard of care. Patients were ineligible for or had refused cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Patients in the comparator arm had a radical cystectomy (surgery to remove the bladder) with or without approved adjuvant treatment.

These results will be presented today in a Proffered Paper session during Presidential Symposium I at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in Madrid, Spain (abstract #LBA2).1 They were also simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

In a planned interim analysis, perioperative IMFINZI plus neoadjuvant EV demonstrated a 49% reduction in the risk of disease progression, recurrence, not undergoing surgery or death versus the comparator arm (based on an EFS hazard ratio [HR] of 0.51; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.38-0.67; p<0.0001). Estimated median EFS was not yet reached for the IMFINZI combination versus 12.1 months for the comparator arm. An estimated 64% of patients treated with the IMFINZI combination remained alive and event-free at two years compared to 45% in the comparator arm.

Results from the key secondary endpoint of OS showed that the IMFINZI combination reduced the risk of death by 42% compared to the comparator arm (based on an OS HR of 0.58; 95% CI 0.40-0.83; p=0.0027). Estimated median OS was not yet reached for the IMFINZI combination or comparator arm. An estimated 78% of patients treated with the IMFINZI combination were alive at two years compared to 69% in the comparator arm.

Thomas Powles, MD, Professor, Chair of Barts Cancer Centre, Barts Health NHS Trust, London, UK, and international coordinating investigator for the VOLGA trial, said: “Patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer require life-changing bladder removal surgery. Despite this, the cancer returns in about half of patients. A new regimen of perioperative durvalumab combined with enfortumab vedotin before surgery reduced the risk of death by 42%, with a manageable safety profile. These practice-changing results support this approach as a patient centric, potential new standard of care in this setting.”

Susan Galbraith, Executive Vice President, Oncology Haematology R&D, AstraZeneca, said: “The VOLGA data show that more than three quarters of patients were still alive two years after treatment with the novel regimen of perioperative IMFINZI and neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin, with quality of life maintained, allowing physicians to optimize treatment for patients in this curative-intent setting. These compelling results reinforce the potential for IMFINZI to become the immunotherapy backbone treatment across muscle-invasive and non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.”

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

There are no contraindications for IMFINZI® (durvalumab) or IMJUDO® (tremelimumab-actl).

Severe and Fatal Immune-Mediated Adverse Reactions

Important immune-mediated adverse reactions listed under Warnings and Precautions may not include all possible severe and fatal immune-mediated reactions. Immune-mediated adverse reactions, which may be severe or fatal, can occur in any organ system or tissue. Immune-mediated adverse reactions can occur at any time after starting treatment or after discontinuation. Monitor patients closely for symptoms and signs that may be clinical manifestations of underlying immune-mediated adverse reactions. Evaluate clinical chemistries including liver enzymes, creatinine, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) level, and thyroid function at baseline and before each dose. In cases of suspected immune-mediated adverse reactions, initiate appropriate workup to exclude alternative etiologies, including infection. Institute medical management promptly, including specialty consultation as appropriate. Withhold or permanently discontinue IMFINZI and IMJUDO depending on severity. See USPI Dosing and Administration for specific details. In general, if IMFINZI and IMJUDO requires interruption or discontinuation, administer systemic corticosteroid therapy (1 mg to 2 mg/kg/day prednisone or equivalent) until improvement to Grade 1 or less. Upon improvement to Grade 1 or less, initiate corticosteroid taper and continue to taper over at least 1 month. Consider administration of other systemic immunosuppressants in patients whose immune-mediated adverse reactions are not controlled with corticosteroid therapy.

Immune-Mediated Pneumonitis

IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated pneumonitis, which may be fatal. The incidence of pneumonitis is higher in patients who have received prior thoracic radiation.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • In patients who did not receive recent prior radiation, the incidence of immune-mediated pneumonitis was 2.4% (34/1414), including fatal (<0.1%), and Grade 3-4 (0.4%) adverse reactions.

    • In patients who received recent prior radiation, the incidence of pneumonitis (including radiation pneumonitis) in patients with unresectable Stage III NSCLC following definitive chemoradiation within 42 days prior to initiation of IMFINZI in PACIFIC was 18.3% (87/475) in patients receiving IMFINZI and 12.8% (30/234) in patients receiving placebo. Of the patients who received IMFINZI (475), 1.1% were fatal and 2.7% were Grade 3 adverse reactions.

    • The incidence of pneumonitis (including radiation pneumonitis) in patients with LS-SCLC following chemoradiation within 42 days prior to initiation of IMFINZI in ADRIATIC was 14% (37/262) in patients receiving IMFINZI and 6% (16/265) in patients receiving placebo. Of the patients who received IMFINZI (262), 0.4% had a fatal adverse reaction and 2.7% had Grade 3 adverse reactions.

    • The frequency and severity of immune-mediated pneumonitis in patients who did not receive definitive chemoradiation prior to IMFINZI were similar in patients who received IMFINZI as a single agent or with ES-SCLC or BTC when given in combination with chemotherapy.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune‑mediated pneumonitis occurred in 1.3% (5/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including fatal (0.3%) and Grade 3 (0.2%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated pneumonitis occurred in 3.5% (21/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including fatal (0.5%), and Grade 3 (1%) adverse reactions.



Immune-Mediated Colitis

IMFINZI with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy can cause immune-mediated colitis, which may be fatal. IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated colitis that is frequently associated with diarrhea. Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection/reactivation has been reported in patients with corticosteroid-refractory immune-mediated colitis. In cases of corticosteroid-refractory colitis, consider repeating infectious workup to exclude alternative etiologies.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Immune-mediated colitis occurred in 2% (37/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 4 (<0.1%) and Grade 3 (0.4%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune‑mediated colitis or diarrhea occurred in 6% (23/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 3 (3.6%) adverse reactions. Intestinal perforation has been observed in other studies of IMFINZI and IMJUDO.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated colitis occurred in 6.5% (39/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy including fatal (0.2%) and Grade 3 (2.5%) adverse reactions. Intestinal perforation and large intestine perforation were reported in 0.1% of patients.



Immune-Mediated Hepatitis

IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated hepatitis, which may be fatal.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Immune-mediated hepatitis occurred in 2.8% (52/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including fatal (0.2%), Grade 4 (0.3%) and Grade 3 (1.4%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune‑mediated hepatitis occurred in 7.5% (29/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including fatal (0.8%), Grade 4 (0.3%) and Grade 3 (4.1%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated hepatitis occurred in 3.9% (23/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including fatal (0.3%), Grade 4 (0.5%), and Grade 3 (2%) adverse reactions.



Immune-Mediated Endocrinopathies

  • Adrenal Insufficiency: IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause primary or secondary adrenal insufficiency. For Grade 2 or higher adrenal insufficiency, initiate symptomatic treatment, including hormone replacement as clinically indicated.
    • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
      • Immune-mediated adrenal insufficiency occurred in 0.5% (9/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (<0.1%) adverse reactions.



    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
      • Immune-mediated adrenal insufficiency occurred in 1.5% (6/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.



    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
      • Immune-mediated adrenal insufficiency occurred in 2.2% (13/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.8%) adverse reactions.





  • Hypophysitis: IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated hypophysitis. Hypophysitis can present with acute symptoms associated with mass effect such as headache, photophobia, or visual field cuts. Hypophysitis can cause hypopituitarism. Initiate symptomatic treatment including hormone replacement as clinically indicated.
    • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
      • Grade 3 hypophysitis/hypopituitarism occurred in <0.1% (1/1889) of patients who received IMFINZI.



    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
      • Immune-mediated hypophysitis/hypopituitarism occurred in 1% (4/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO.



    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
      • Immune-mediated hypophysitis occurred in 1.3% (8/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.5%) adverse reactions.





  • Thyroid Disorders: IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated thyroid disorders. Thyroiditis can present with or without endocrinopathy. Hypothyroidism can follow hyperthyroidism. Initiate hormone replacement therapy for hypothyroidism or institute medical management of hyperthyroidism as clinically indicated.
    • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
      • Immune-mediated thyroiditis occurred in 0.5% (9/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (<0.1%) adverse reactions.

      • Immune-mediated hyperthyroidism occurred in 2.1% (39/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI.

      • Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 8.3% (156/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (<0.1%) adverse reactions.



    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
      • Immune-mediated thyroiditis occurred in 1.5% (6/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO.

      • Immune-mediated hyperthyroidism occurred in 4.6% (18/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.

      • Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 11% (42/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO.



    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
      • Immune-mediated thyroiditis occurred in 1.2% (7/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy.

      • Immune-mediated hyperthyroidism occurred in 5% (30/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.2%) adverse reactions.

      • Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 8.6% (51/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.5%) adverse reactions.



    • IMFINZI with Carboplatin and Paclitaxel
      • Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 14% (34/235) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel.





  • Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, which can present with diabetic ketoacidosis: Monitor patients for hyperglycemia or other signs and symptoms of diabetes. Initiate treatment with insulin as clinically indicated.
    • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
      • Grade 3 immune-mediated Type 1 diabetes mellitus occurred in <0.1% (1/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI.



    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
      • Two patients (0.5%, 2/388) had events of hyperglycemia requiring insulin therapy that had not resolved at last follow-up.



    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
      • Immune-mediated Type 1 diabetes mellitus occurred in 0.5% (3/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.





Immune-Mediated Nephritis with Renal Dysfunction

IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated nephritis.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Immune-mediated nephritis occurred in 0.5% (10/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (<0.1%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune-mediated nephritis occurred in 1% (4/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 3 (0.5%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated nephritis occurred in 0.7% (4/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.2%) adverse reactions.



Immune-Mediated Dermatology Reactions

IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated rash or dermatitis. Exfoliative dermatitis, including Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), has occurred with PD-1/L-1 and CTLA-4 blocking antibodies. Topical emollients and/or topical corticosteroids may be adequate to treat mild to moderate non-exfoliative rashes.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Immune-mediated rash or dermatitis occurred in 1.8% (34/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (0.4%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune-mediated rash or dermatitis occurred in 4.9% (19/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 4 (0.3%) and Grade 3 (1.5%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated rash or dermatitis occurred in 7.2% (43/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.



Immune-Mediated Pancreatitis

IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated pancreatitis. Immune-mediated pancreatitis occurred in 2.3% (9/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 4 (0.3%) and Grade 3 (1.5%) adverse reactions.

Other Immune-Mediated Adverse Reactions

The following clinically significant, immune-mediated adverse reactions occurred at an incidence of less than 1% each in patients who received IMFINZI and IMJUDO or were reported with the use of other immune-checkpoint inhibitors.

  • Cardiac/vascular: Myocarditis, pericarditis, vasculitis.

  • Nervous system: Meningitis, encephalitis, myelitis and demyelination, myasthenic syndrome/myasthenia gravis (including exacerbation), Guillain-Barré syndrome, nerve paresis, autoimmune neuropathy.

  • Ocular: Uveitis, iritis, and other ocular inflammatory toxicities can occur. Some cases can be associated with retinal detachment. Various grades of visual impairment to include blindness can occur. If uveitis occurs in combination with other immune-mediated adverse reactions, consider a Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada-like syndrome, as this may require treatment with systemic steroids to reduce the risk of permanent vision loss.

  • Gastrointestinal: Pancreatitis including increases in serum amylase and lipase levels, gastritis, duodenitis.

  • Musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders: Myositis/polymyositis, rhabdomyolysis and associated sequelae including renal failure, arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica.

  • Endocrine: Hypoparathyroidism.

  • Hematologic/Immune: Hemolytic anemia, aplastic anemia, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, systemic inflammatory response syndrome, histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis (Kikuchi lymphadenitis), sarcoidosis, immune thrombocytopenia, solid organ transplant rejection, other transplant (including corneal graft) rejection.

  • Other: Myocarditis-Myositis-Myasthenia Gravis (or Myasthenia-Like) Overlap Syndrome, reported as the co-occurrence of either two or all three adverse reactions

Infusion-Related Reactions

IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause severe or life-threatening infusion-related reactions. Monitor for signs and symptoms of infusion-related reactions. Interrupt, slow the rate of, or permanently discontinue IMFINZI and IMJUDO based on the severity. See USPI Dosing and Administration for specific details. For Grade 1 or 2 infusion-related reactions, consider using pre-medications with subsequent doses.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Infusion-related reactions occurred in 2.2% (42/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Infusion-related reactions occurred in 2.6% (10/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO.



  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Infusion-related reactions occurred in 2.9% (17/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.



Complications of Allogeneic HSCT after IMFINZI

Fatal and other serious complications can occur in patients who receive allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) before or after being treated with a PD-1/L-1 blocking antibody. Transplant-related complications include hyperacute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), acute GVHD, chronic GVHD, hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD) after reduced intensity conditioning, and steroid-requiring febrile syndrome (without an identified infectious cause). These complications may occur despite intervening therapy between PD-1/L-1 blockade and allogeneic HSCT. Follow patients closely for evidence of transplant-related complications and intervene promptly. Consider the benefit versus risks of treatment with a PD-1/L-1 blocking antibody prior to or after an allogeneic HSCT.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity

Based on their mechanism of action and data from animal studies, IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus. In females of reproductive potential, verify pregnancy status prior to initiating IMFINZI and IMJUDO and advise them to use effective contraception during treatment with IMFINZI and IMJUDO and for 3 months after the last dose of IMFINZI and IMJUDO.

Lactation

There is no information regarding the presence of IMFINZI and IMJUDO in human milk; however, because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants from IMFINZI and IMJUDO, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose.

Adverse Reactions

Unresectable Stage III NSCLC

  • In patients with Stage III NSCLC in the PACIFIC study receiving IMFINZI (n=475), the most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were cough (40%), fatigue (34%), pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis (34%), upper respiratory tract infections (26%), dyspnea (25%), and rash (23%). The most common Grade 3 or 4 adverse reactions (≥3%) were pneumonia (7%) and pneumonitis/radiation pneumonitis (3.4%).

  • In patients with Stage III NSCLC in the PACIFIC study receiving IMFINZI (n=475), discontinuation due to adverse reactions occurred in 15% of patients in the IMFINZI arm. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 29% of patients receiving IMFINZI. The most frequent serious adverse reactions (≥2%) were pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis (7%) and pneumonia (6%). Fatal pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis and fatal pneumonia occurred in <2% of patients and were similar across arms.

Resectable NSCLC

  • In patients with resectable NSCLC in the AEGEAN study, the most common adverse reactions (occurring in ≥20% of patients) were anemia, nausea, constipation, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, and rash.

  • In patients with resectable NSCLC in the neoadjuvant phase of the AEGEAN study receiving IMFINZI in combination with platinum-containing chemotherapy (n=401), permanent discontinuation of IMFINZI due to an adverse reaction occurred in 6.7% of patients. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 21% of patients. The most frequent (≥1%) serious adverse reactions were pneumonia (2.7%), anemia (1.5%), myelosuppression (1.5%), vomiting (1.2%), neutropenia (1%), and acute kidney injury (1%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 2% of patients, including death due to COVID-19 pneumonia (0.5%), sepsis (0.5%), myocarditis (0.2%), decreased appetite (0.2%), hemoptysis (0.2%), and death not otherwise specified (0.2%). Of the 401 IMFINZI-treated patients who received neoadjuvant treatment and 398 placebo-treated patients who received neoadjuvant treatment, 1.7% (n=7) and 1% (n=4), respectively, did not receive surgery due to adverse reactions.

  • In patients with resectable NSCLC in the adjuvant phase of the AEGEAN study receiving IMFINZI as a single agent (n=265), permanent discontinuation of IMFINZI due to an adverse reaction occurred in 8% of patients. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 13% of patients. The most frequent serious adverse reactions reported in >1% of patients were pneumonia (1.9%), pneumonitis (1.1%), and COVID-19 (1.1%). Four fatal adverse reactions occurred during the adjuvant phase of the study, including COVID-19 pneumonia, pneumonia aspiration, interstitial lung disease and aortic aneurysm.

Metastatic NSCLC

  • In patients with mNSCLC in the POSEIDON study receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO plus platinum-based chemotherapy (n=330), the most common adverse reactions (occurring in ≥20% of patients) were nausea (42%), fatigue (36%), musculoskeletal pain (29%), decreased appetite (28%), rash (27%), and diarrhea (22%).

  • In patients with mNSCLC in the POSEIDON study receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy (n=330), permanent discontinuation of IMFINZI or IMJUDO due to an adverse reaction occurred in 17% of patients. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 44% of patients, with the most frequent serious adverse reactions reported in at least 2% of patients being pneumonia (11%), anemia (5%), diarrhea (2.4%), thrombocytopenia (2.4%), pyrexia (2.4%), and febrile neutropenia (2.1%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in a total of 4.2% of patients.

Limited-stage Small Cell Lung Cancer

  • In patients with limited-stage SCLC in the ADRIATIC study receiving IMFINZI (n=262), the most common adverse reactions occurring in ≥20% of patients receiving IMFINZI were pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis (38%), and fatigue (21%). The most common Grade 3 or 4 adverse reactions (≥3%) were pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis and pneumonia.

  • In patients with limited-stage SCLC in the ADRIATIC study receiving IMFINZI (n=262), IMFINZI was permanently discontinued due to adverse reactions in 16% of the patients receiving IMFINZI. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 30% of patients receiving IMFINZI. The most frequent serious adverse reactions reported in ≥1% of patients receiving IMFINZI were pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis (12%), and pneumonia (5%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 2.7% of patients who received IMFINZI including pneumonia (1.5%), cardiac failure, encephalopathy and pneumonitis (0.4% each).

Extensive-stage Small Cell Lung Cancer

  • In patients with extensive-stage SCLC in the CASPIAN study receiving IMFINZI plus chemotherapy (n=265), the most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were nausea (34%), fatigue/asthenia (32%), and alopecia (31%). The most common Grade 3 or 4 adverse reaction (≥3%) was fatigue/asthenia (3.4%).

  • In patients with extensive-stage SCLC in the CASPIAN study receiving IMFINZI plus chemotherapy (n=265), IMFINZI was discontinued due to adverse reactions in 7% of the patients receiving IMFINZI plus chemotherapy. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 31% of patients receiving IMFINZI plus chemotherapy. The most frequent serious adverse reactions reported in at least 1% of patients were febrile neutropenia (4.5%), pneumonia (2.3%), anemia (1.9%), pancytopenia (1.5%), pneumonitis (1.1%), and COPD (1.1%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4.9% of patients receiving IMFINZI plus chemotherapy.

Locally Advanced or Metastatic Biliary Tract Cancers (BTCs)

  • In patients with locally advanced or metastatic BTCs in the TOPAZ-1 study receiving IMFINZI (n=338), the most common adverse reactions (occurring in ≥20% of patients) were fatigue (42%), nausea (40%), constipation (32%), decreased appetite (26%), abdominal pain (24%), rash (23%), and pyrexia (20%).

  • In patients with locally advanced or metastatic BTCs in the TOPAZ-1 study receiving IMFINZI (n=338), discontinuation due to adverse reactions occurred in 6% of the patients receiving IMFINZI plus chemotherapy. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 47% of patients receiving IMFINZI plus chemotherapy. The most frequent serious adverse reactions reported in at least 2% of patients were cholangitis (7%), pyrexia (3.8%), anemia (3.6%), sepsis (3.3%), and acute kidney injury (2.4%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 3.6% of patients receiving IMFINZI plus chemotherapy. These include ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke (4 patients), sepsis (2 patients), and upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage (2 patients).

Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC)

  • In patients with unresectable HCC in the HIMALAYA study receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO (n=388), the most common adverse reactions (occurring in ≥20% of patients) were rash (32%), diarrhea (27%), fatigue (26%), pruritus (23%), musculoskeletal pain (22%), and abdominal pain (20%).

  • In patients with unresectable HCC in the HIMALAYA study receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO (n=388), serious adverse reactions occurred in 41% of patients. Serious adverse reactions in >1% of patients included hemorrhage (6%), diarrhea (4%), sepsis (2.1%), pneumonia (2.1%), rash (1.5%), vomiting (1.3%), acute kidney injury (1.3%), and anemia (1.3%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 8% of patients who received IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including death (1%), hemorrhage intracranial (0.5%), cardiac arrest (0.5%), pneumonitis (0.5%), hepatic failure (0.5%), and immune-mediated hepatitis (0.5%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 30% of patients who received IMFINZI with carboplatin and paclitaxel; the most common serious adverse reactions (≥4%) were constipation (4.5%) and rash (4.5%).

  • In patients with BCG-naive, HR-NMIBC in the POTOMAC study receiving IMFINZI in combination with BCG, the most common (≥20%) adverse reactions, including laboratory abnormalities were increased glucose (43%), increased AST (43%), increased lipase (42%), increased ALT (42%), increased GGT (40%), urinary tract infection (40%), increased potassium (39%), dysuria (37%), decreased hemoglobin (35%), hematuria (33%), increased serum creatinine (30%), musculoskeletal pain (28%), decreased lymphocytes (27%), urinary frequency (26%), decreased sodium (23%), fatigue (21%), rash (20%), and pyrexia (20%).

  • In patients with BCG-naive, HR-NMIBC in the POTOMAC study receiving IMFINZI in combination with BCG, permanent discontinuation of IMFINZI due to adverse reactions occurred in 18% of patients. The adverse reactions which resulted in permanent discontinuation of IMFINZI (≥1%) were hepatitis (1.8%), acute kidney injury (1.2%), and diarrhea (1.2%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 32% of patients. The most common (≥1%) serious adverse reactions were urinary tract infection (4.5%), COVID (1.8%), hepatitis (1.5%), dysuria (1.2%), and prostate cancer (1.2%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 2.4% of patients who received IMFINZI in combination with BCG, including congestive cardiac failure (0.6%), COVID (0.3%), cardiovascular disorder (0.3%), dementia with Lewy bodies (0.3%), and pancreatic cancer (0.3%).

Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer (MIBC)

  • In patients with MIBC, the most common adverse reactions, including laboratory abnormalities, in the overall study (occurring in ≥20% of patients) were decreased hemoglobin, decreased neutrophils, increased blood creatinine, decreased sodium, nausea, increased ALT, decreased calcium, decreased platelets, fatigue, increased potassium, decreased lymphocytes, increased AST, constipation, decreased magnesium, decreased appetite, increased alkaline phosphatase, rash, pyrexia, diarrhea, vomiting and abdominal pain.

  • In patients with MIBC in the neoadjuvant phase of the NIAGARA study receiving IMFINZI in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin (n=530), permanent discontinuation of IMFINZI due to an adverse reaction occurred in 9% of patients. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 24% of patients; the most frequent (≥1%) serious adverse reactions were pulmonary embolism (1.9%), febrile neutropenia (1.5%), acute kidney injury (1.3%), thrombocytopenia (1.3%), urinary tract infection (1.3%), and pneumonia (1.3%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1.1% of patients including sepsis, myocardial infarction, and pulmonary embolism (0.2% each). One fatal adverse reaction of pneumonia was reported in 1 (0.2%) patient in the post-surgery phase before adjuvant treatment started. Of the 530 patients in the IMFINZI treatment arm and 526 patients in the chemotherapy treatment arm who received neoadjuvant treatment, 1 (0.2%) patient in each treatment arm did not receive surgery due to adverse reactions. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 26% of patients. The most frequent serious adverse reactions (occurring in ≥1% of patients) were urinary tract infection (7%), acute kidney injury (3.7%), hydronephrosis (2.1%), pyelonephritis (2.1%), urosepsis (1.8%) and sepsis (1.6%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1.8% of patients, including COVID-19, severe acute respiratory syndrome, cardiopulmonary failure, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and chronic hepatic failure (0.3% each).
